summary.headline: Onward Technologies Q2 FY27 revenue hit a record INR170.2 crore (+22.4% YoY), EBITDA margin 15.6%, and FY27 guidance was raised to 15-18% growth.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 revenue reached a record INR170.2 crore, up 22.4% YoY and 13.9% QoQ, with constant-currency growth of 17.7% YoY and 13.5% QoQ. EBITDA rose 33.7% YoY to INR26.6 crore at a record 15.6% margin, and PAT grew 41.2% YoY to INR16.8 crore. Margin gains were helped by an INR2.9 crore UK R&D credit relating to FY26, which management booked in Q2 after approval in September. Management raised FY27 revenue growth guidance to 15-18% and EBITDA margin guidance to 13.8-14.3%, replacing the earlier "double-digit" language. Receivable days stretched to about 80, which management attributed to fast growth and customer approval delays.

segments.name: Industrial
segments.commentary: Management described industrial as the most dominant and most mature vertical; an analyst noted roughly 20% growth for eight quarters, which management did not dispute. Customers in manufacturing are growing rapidly, including on AI data center work.

segments.name: Transportation & Mobility (T&M)
segments.commentary: Management said automotive is recovering from the prior year's furloughs and shutdowns, mainly in Europe, while rail has grown meaningfully for several quarters. Management expects T&M to grow much faster over the next couple of quarters, but gave no figures.

segments.name: Healthcare & Life Sciences (HCLS)
segments.commentary: Revenue is small, around INR5 crore a quarter per an analyst's estimate. Management said the vertical is still waiting for large programme wins, and expects it to ramp similarly to the other verticals.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth guidance raised to 15-18% (from prior outlook); management said the revision is post the new US regulatory environment.
FY27 EBITDA margin guidance set at 13.8-14.3%, replacing the earlier 'double-digit' EBITDA language.
Q3 hiring to be slower due to the holiday period, with focus on subject matter experts for 2027-28; Q4 to add another few hundred net people.
Receivable days expected to normalise to the 65-70 day sweet spot within the next 2 quarters.
Unbilled receivables expected to normalise in Q3 and Q4 FY27 after PO and payment delays.
Chennai AI lab expected to be up and running by Q4 FY27 or early 2027, with first benefit in 2027.
capex_capacity: Net hiring of about 430-450 employees in H1 FY27 across four Indian delivery centres (Pune, Chennai, Bengaluru, Hyderabad); total headcount about 3,000-plus.
Fourth design centre in Pune opened in October 2026, expected to reach full capacity by end-November/December; lease signed for additional seats in Pune.
Chennai AI lab under construction with hiring underway.
Office purchased in Worli, Mumbai, which contributed to the rise in depreciation.
Management said it has substantial cash reserves to invest ahead of customer engagements.
demand_pricing: Renewed 3-year digital engineering contract worth about INR44.5 crore with a global construction and mining equipment leader; contract value up over 70% versus the prior term. The customer awarded the full contract rather than 6-month or annual SOWs.
Customers billing $1 million or more annually rose from 16 to 18 in the quarter.
Management is bidding on several large RFPs with existing customers, with opportunities in AI-led transformation, data center infrastructure engineering, power management and cooling systems.
Management says it has 70-plus customers, all in US and Europe; it has no India customers. Aspiration is about $10 million annual revenue per customer.
Management said AI so far is reducing neither engineering workload nor billing; it expects productivity pressure over time and included some AI impact in the revised guidance.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the guidance upgrade and what visibility supports 15-18%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited H1 execution, visibility from existing North American customers, net hiring of about 430-plus people in six months, and RFQs tied to AI data center demand.

qa_highlights.question: What is the impact of the new US visa and PERM rules on onsite delivery?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is cautious, is hiring local people in the US, and the guidance already reflects the new regulatory environment.

qa_highlights.question: Why did unbilled receivables rise and when will they convert to cash?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said a fast ramp-up, delayed POs and delayed customer payments caused it; September was one of the highest months, and normalisation is expected in Q3 and Q4.

qa_highlights.question: What is the nature and timing of the INR2.9 crore R&D credit?
qa_highlights.answer: It is a UK R&D credit for FY26, available annually at about 10-15% of revenue, approved in September, booked net of employee costs, and reported as a special line item.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the margin expansion?
qa_highlights.answer: Higher offshore utilisation, improved offshore leverage as customers ramped offshore faster, delivery discipline on a few key customers, and training investments.

qa_highlights.question: Is there upside to guidance and what limits wallet share gains?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it prefers to stay prudent; execution and ramp speed, along with capacity (people and infrastructure), are the constraints rather than demand.

qa_highlights.question: What is the hiring plan for the next two quarters?
qa_highlights.answer: Q3 hiring will be slower due to holidays, with offers out and SME hiring prioritised; Q4 and Q1 will add a few hundred net people.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for Healthcare and T&M?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects T&M to grow faster over the next couple of quarters, and HCLS to ramp like other verticals once large programmes are won.

qa_highlights.question: How does AI affect pricing and revenue per employee?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said AI productivity is not yet causing pushback; revenue per employee is an aspirational INR35-40 lakh, blended 10% onsite and 90% offshore, and is not the current guidance basis.

qa_highlights.question: Why did receivable days rise to about 80 and what is the target?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to fast growth and delays in customer approvals, with a target of 65-70 days and normalisation expected in the next two quarters.

risks_watch: Receivable days at about 80 versus a 65-70 day target; unbilled receivables still elevated until Q3/Q4.
US visa and PERM rules affecting onsite delivery and local hiring costs.
Q3 seasonal hiring slowdown and a competitive hiring market, with design centres near full capacity.
AI-driven productivity could pressure revenue per engineer over time, per an analyst.
Execution risk on a rapid ramp and external delays to projects, which management acknowledged.
Depreciation rise and higher costs from new hires and the Worli office purchase.
summary.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on growth and margins, but measured on the forward outlook: management said it prefers to stay prudent and attributed constraints to execution and capacity rather than demand. It was candid about working-capital strain and US immigration impact, and was evasive on the segment-wise constant-currency split, deferring that to the IR team.

growth.why: FY27 revenue growth guided up to 15-18% (midpoint 16.5%), backed by a INR44.5 crore three-year renewal with 70%+ higher contract value, customers at $1M+ rising from 16 to 18, and ~430-450 net hires plus a new Pune centre; no specific capacity-to-revenue numbers were given, and the Q2 EBITDA growth includes a one-time INR2.9 crore UK R&D credit.
